arms.better: The agent found the right ignore and walker files quickly, but spent repeated cycles re-reading walker code and never stated a clear plan before the provider stopped the run. tm's progress output said `Ticket T-1 dispatched for execution.` three times, which looks like duplicate work without explaining a retry/attempt number; the actual stopping message did identify HTTP 429 and suggested `tm ticket retry T-1`, but the preceding `Ran a command -> error: couldn't find that` hides the failed operation and gives the user no diagnostic. The run produced no patch or verification, and tokens were unavailable in the plain `tm events` output. A clearer one-time dispatch message with attempt/retry context, actionable command errors that retain a concise cause, and a surfaced token total would make this easier to trust and recover from.

OpenCode traced the cache reuse to `Ignore::add_parents`, produced a focused fix and regression coverage for both root orders and sequential/parallel walking, and reported the focused and package-level test runs. One early semantic-search tool attempt failed because the clone had no zvec index; it fell back to exact search and continued. The final test checkout overwrote `dir.rs`, which contains both production changes and inline tests, so the required post-run test result is mechanically passing but is not an independent check of the agent's final patch. A more reliable protocol would separate the fix's tests from production code or otherwise apply only test hunks when the merged PR bundles them in one file.
